question: Should OpenClaw core add first-party per-agent backup/restore/clone semantics, and what credential/session portability policy should those archives use?
rationale: The feature touches core persisted state, restore semantics, credentials, transcripts, and archive compatibility; code inspection shows no existing contract that automation can safely infer.

options.title: Design guarded core restore/clone
options.body: Define the archive manifest, credential/session portability rules, path rewrite behavior, rollback policy, and tests before inviting or queuing implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader backup restore work
options.body: Make this a requirement of the broader backup/restore or encrypted snapshot project so one archive format owns both whole-instance and per-agent restore.

options.title: Defer per-agent clone
options.body: Keep whole-instance backups only and document manual export/import constraints until maintainers are ready to own per-agent restore safety.

recommendation.title: Design guarded core restore/clone
recommendation.body: Define the archive manifest, credential/session portability rules, path rewrite behavior, rollback policy, and tests before inviting or queuing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup-area history plus maintainer-side product/security routing make this the best available owner from the evidence set.
